text.p: Singapore shares returned to an even keel by Tuesday's close after Monday's sharp falls, but dealers said the calmer day did not herald a full recovery.
"The real news that's going to get the money back into Singapore is good results numbers, but we're not going to see those in the coming crop of interims," one dealer said.
Predicting further consolidation, another dealer said a rise in manufacturing output revealed on Tuesday was positive for the market, "but they're only the start".
The blue chip-tracking Straits Times Industrials Index ended almost unchanged, down 0.40 of a point to 1,893.46.
Singapore shares have been under pressure from poor results expectations, regional currency woes and worries over the possible merger of some domestic and foreign share tranche listings.
Some stability returned to foreign shares on Tuesday as the Stock Exchange of Singapore's foreign share index ended up 4.51 at 144.87.
Singapore Press foreign rose Singapore $0.70 to S$26.50, SIA foreign climbed S$0.50 to S$12.10 and DBS foreign gained S$0.30 to S$17.40.
Mainly Malaysian over-the-counter traded shares were Tuesday's main casulaties, reflecting sharp falls in Kuala Lumpur. The UOB OTC index dropped 8.83 points to 987.97.
